Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to velvety brown-black fungal spots on upper leaf surfaces and fruit lesions.
Apple___Apple_scab.organic_treatment: Apply neem oil, liquid copper soap, or sulfur sprays early in the season. Rake and destroy fallen leaves to reduce overwintering spores.
Apple___Apple_scab.chemical_treatment: Fungicides containing Captan, Mancozeb, or Myclobutanil at bud break and petal fall.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Prune tree canopies to improve air circulation and sunlight penetration; plant scab-resistant apple cultivars.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Small purple leaf spots that enlarge into 'frog-eye' circles with light centers; dark, sunken rot on fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.organic_treatment: Prune out dead or diseased twigs, mummified fruits, and cankers at least 15 cm below infected tissue. Burn or bury infected debris.
Apple___Black_rot.chemical_treatment: Captan or Thiophanate-methyl applications starting at silver tip through harvest intervals.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Ensure good air circulation, remove wild apple or brambles near orchard, and sanitize pruning shears between cuts.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange or rusty spots on leaves; small tube-like spore structures forming on the leaf underside.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.organic_treatment: Apply sulfur or copper sprays when apple blossom buds first show pink color.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.chemical_treatment: Immunox or Myclobutanil fungicides applied from pink bud stage through early summer.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Remove nearby eastern red cedar trees or galls within 500-1000 feet of the orchard if feasible.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Lush, uniformly green foliage with no fungal lesions, chlorosis, or necrotic spots.
Apple___healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain regular balanced organic fertilization (compost or compost tea) and consistent soil moisture.
Apple___healthy.chemical_treatment: None required. Routine dormant oil spray may be applied for overwintering pests.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Continue seasonal pruning, mulch around the drip line, and monitor for early pest signs.

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green leaves, well-formed leaf margins without rust or scorch.
Blueberry___healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5 to 5.2) using elemental sulfur or peat moss; provide steady drip irrigation.
Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Mulch with pine bark, maintain soil acidity, and avoid overhead sprinkler watering.

Cherry___healthy.symptoms: Uniformly green, firm cherry foliage with no spots, powdery mildew, or shot-hole perforations.
Cherry___healthy.organic_treatment: Maintain adequate tree nutrition with well-decomposed organic manure and consistent irrigation.
Cherry___healthy.prevention: Perform winter pruning for canopy airflow and keep the orchard floor clean.

Cherry___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery fungal coating on leaves and young shoots, causing leaf curling and distorted growth.
Cherry___Powdery_mildew.organic_treatment: Spray with potassium bicarbonate, dilute milk solution (1:9), or horticultural mineral oil.
Cherry___Powdery_mildew.chemical_treatment: Apply Quinoxyfen, Triflumizole, or Myclobutanil fungicides at early onset.
Cherry___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer which causes rapid susceptible succulent growth; maintain open canopy pruning.

Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.symptoms: Narrow, rectangular lesions bordered by leaf veins, turning tan or gray as fungal spores mature.
Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.organic_treatment: Practice crop rotation with non-host crops (soybeans, alfalfa); chop and bury corn residue post-harvest.
Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.chemical_treatment: Apply strobilurin (Azoxystrobin) or triazole (Propiconazole) foliar fungicides at tassel emergence.
Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray_leaf_sp.prevention: Select resistant corn hybrids; manage residue through conventional tillage if disease pressure is severe.

Corn___Common_rust.symptoms: Oval, reddish-brown pustules scattered over both upper and lower leaf surfaces that rupture the epidermis.
Corn___Common_rust.organic_treatment: Plant rust-resistant hybrids; apply early biological controls such as Bacillus subtilis.
Corn___Common_rust.chemical_treatment: Foliar fungicides (Pyraclostrobin, Fluxapyroxad) applied if rust covers >5% of ear leaf before silking.
Corn___Common_rust.prevention: Early planting helps crops mature before high spore flights arrive in cooler, humid weather.

Corn___healthy.symptoms: Broad, vibrant deep-green leaves with crisp parallel veins and no pustules or blights.
Corn___healthy.organic_treatment: Provide adequate nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium according to soil test recommendations.
Corn___healthy.prevention: Maintain proper plant spacing (approx 30,000 plants/acre) and weed-free field borders.

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2.5 - 15 cm long) on corn leaves.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.organic_treatment: Deep-till infected crop residue after harvest; rotate fields with soybeans for at least 1-2 seasons.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.chemical_treatment: Fungicide mixtures containing Strobilurins and Triazoles applied between V12 and R1 growth stages.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Plant hybrids possessing Ht resistance genes; monitor during prolonged periods of heavy dew and mild temperatures.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Small, reddish-brown circular spots on leaves; shriveling and blackening of grape berries into hard mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.organic_treatment: Spray wettable sulfur or copper hydroxide before rainfall periods during early shoot development.
Grape___Black_rot.chemical_treatment: Myclobutanil, Mancozeb, or Ziram sprays starting at 1-3 inch shoot growth and repeating every 10-14 days.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Prune out mummified clusters during winter dormancy; trellis vines to maximize sunlight and rapid leaf drying.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' leaf patterns with interveinal chlorosis and necrosis; dark sunken spots on berries.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).organic_treatment: Paint wound sealant or Trichoderma biological protectants on all large pruning cuts immediately.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).chemical_treatment: No curative chemical exists once trunk infection occurs; protect fresh pruning wounds with Thiophanate-methyl.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Delay pruning until late winter when wound susceptibility is lower; avoid pruning in rainy, humid conditions.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Smooth, well-developed lobed foliage with no discoloration, necrosis, or mildew growth.
Grape___healthy.organic_treatment: Ensure well-drained soil, balanced organic amendments, and proper canopy management.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Maintain annual dormant pruning and canopy shoot positioning.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular brown patches on leaves with dark borders; premature leaf yellowing and shedding.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.organic_treatment: Apply copper-based fungicides (Bordeaux mixture) or sulfur dusting in humid weather.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.chemical_treatment: Broad-spectrum fungicides such as Mancozeb or Chlorothalonil.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Collect and burn fallen leaves in the autumn; thin dense canopy to improve ventilation.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Asymmetrical blotchy mottle leaf yellowing; vein corking; lopsided, bitter fruit that stays green at base.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).organic_treatment: Control Asian Citrus Psyllid (ACP) vectors with horticultural oil and biological parasitoid wasps (Tamarixia radiata).
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).chemical_treatment: Systemic insecticides (Imidacloprid, Thiamethoxam) to suppress psyllid populations; foliar micronutrient sprays.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Plant only certified disease-free nursery stock; immediately remove and destroy infected trees to safeguard the grove.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small angular water-soaked leaf spots turning purple-brown; centers fall out leaving a 'shot-hole' appearance.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.organic_treatment: Apply fixed copper bactericides from dormant bud stage until bloom; avoid excessive copper after petal fall.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.chemical_treatment: Oxytetracycline (Mycoshield) applied weekly during wet spring periods from shuck-split onward.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars (e.g., Redhaven, Biscoe); avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.

Peach___healthy.symptoms: Clean, elongated lanceolate leaves with glossy green texture and zero shot-hole lesions.
Peach___healthy.organic_treatment: Apply composted mulch under dripline; maintain regular deep watering at soil level.
Peach___healthy.prevention: Sanitize pruning tools and conduct seasonal checks for peach tree borers.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, circular to irregular lesions on leaves that turn dark brown; extensive defoliation.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.organic_treatment: Treat seeds with hot water (50°C for 25 min); spray copper octanoate combined with Bacillus subtilis.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.chemical_treatment: Copper hydroxide mixed with Mancozeb spray every 7-10 days during warm, rainy weather.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds; implement a 2-3 year crop rotation away from solanaceous plants.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Vigorous, dark green leaves with uniform surface texture and no spots or curling.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.organic_treatment: Feed with balanced organic vegetable fertilizer high in calcium and magnesium.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Use drip irrigation to keep foliage dry and stake plants for structural support.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with concentric rings creating a 'target board' pattern on older foliage.
Potato___Early_blight.organic_treatment: Spray bio-fungicides containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens or copper sulfate; remove lower infected leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.chemical_treatment: Fungicide programs with Chlorothalonil, Azoxystrobin, or Difenoconazole at initial symptom detection.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation; maintain balanced plant nutrition to avoid plant stress.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Sturdy green compound foliage free of wilting, black spots, or water-soaked blotches.
Potato___healthy.organic_treatment: Hill plants with rich soil and straw mulch; maintain uniform soil moisture.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Plant certified seed tubers and maintain proper spacing for canopy airflow.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked dark lesions with pale green halos; white fungal fuzz on leaf undersides in high humidity.
Potato___Late_blight.organic_treatment: Copper-based fungicides applied preventatively before humid rain spells; immediately destroy infected vines.
Potato___Late_blight.chemical_treatment: Systemic fungicides (Fluopicolide, Mandipropamid, Cymoxanil) applied on a tight schedule.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Eliminate cull potato piles; plant certified blight-free tubers; avoid overhead irrigation.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Compound serrated leaves of deep green color with white-pubescent undersides, completely free of spots.
Raspberry___healthy.organic_treatment: Mulch with wood chips; provide trellising for cane airflow; feed with organic compost in spring.
Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Prune spent floricanes right after fruiting to keep the patch aerated.

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Trifoliate leaves exhibiting healthy rich green color without mosaic patterns, rust, or pustules.
Soybean___healthy.organic_treatment: Inoculate seeds with Rhizobium bacteria for optimal atmospheric nitrogen fixation.
Soybean___healthy.prevention: Rotate crops with corn or small grains; scout weekly for defoliating insects.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: Powdery white talcum-like spots spreading over both upper and lower leaf surfaces, leading to early leaf senescence.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.organic_treatment: Spray neem oil, potassium bicarbonate (3g/L with surfactant), or bio-fungicide (Bacillus subtilis).
Squash___Powdery_mildew.chemical_treatment: Fungicides like Myclobutanil or Trifloxystrobin applied at first trace of mildew.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Select resistant squash varieties; plant in full sun and space vines adequately.

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Trifoliate, serrated leaves with glossy dark-green upper surfaces and no scorching or purpling.
Strawberry___healthy.organic_treatment: Mulch strawberry beds with clean pine straw or black plastic; ensure crown is planted at soil level.
Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Renovate strawberry beds after harvest and remove old senescent leaves.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Numerous small, irregular purple-to-dark brown blotches without clear white centers; leaves wither and curl as if burned.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.organic_treatment: Apply copper fungicides in early spring; remove heavily infected foliage after harvest renovation.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.chemical_treatment: Foliar applications of Captan or Pyraclostrobin during spring flush.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen in spring; maintain weed-free beds to speed leaf drying.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, greasy water-soaked spots with yellow halos on leaves; scabby raised lesions on green fruit.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.organic_treatment: Treat seeds with 1.3% sodium hypochlorite or hot water; spray copper hydroxide combined with Bacillus subtilis.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.chemical_treatment: Copper octanoate tank-mixed with Mancozeb applied every 7 days in humid weather.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Avoid working in the tomato patch while plants are wet; practice 2-year crop rotation.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots on lowest leaves with characteristic concentric concentric target rings, followed by yellowing.
Tomato___Early_blight.organic_treatment: Prune all bottom leaves up to 12 inches above the soil line; apply liquid copper or sulfur sprays weekly.
Tomato___Early_blight.chemical_treatment: Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Azoxystrobin preventative sprays.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Apply thick straw mulch to prevent soil splashing onto foliage; water strictly at ground level with drip irrigation.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Crisp, fragrant, deep green compound foliage without blemishes, spots, wilting, or yellowing.
Tomato___healthy.organic_treatment: Feed with balanced tomato fertilizer containing calcium (to prevent blossom end rot); mulch heavily.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Stake or cage plants off the ground and maintain adequate spacing.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark greasy-gray blotches that turn brown and papery; white cottony mildew under leaves in wet conditions; rapid plant collapse.
Tomato___Late_blight.organic_treatment: Preventative copper fungicide before rain; immediately pull and bag entire infected plants; do NOT compost.
Tomato___Late_blight.chemical_treatment: Targeted fungicides: Mandipropamid (Revus), Cyazofamid (Ranman), or Chlorothalonil.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Grow late-blight-resistant varieties (e.g. Mountain Magic, Defiant); avoid planting near potatoes.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces; velvety olive-green to brown fungal growth underneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.organic_treatment: Lower greenhouse humidity below 85%; apply copper or biofungicide (Trichoderma harzianum).
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Maximize air ventilation using fans in greenhouses; avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous circular spots (1-3 mm) with dark brown margins and sunken gray/tan centers speckled with tiny black dots.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.organic_treatment: Pinch off infected lower leaves immediately; spray copper soap fungicide every 7 days.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.chemical_treatment: Foliar treatments with Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Quadris.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Use straw mulch beneath plants to stop spore splashing from soil; clean tomato cages with 10% bleach solution.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow or white stippling on leaf surfaces; delicate webbing on leaf undersides and growing tips.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.organic_treatment: Spray insecticidal soap, neem oil, or rosemary essential oil; release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis).
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.chemical_treatment: Miticides such as Bifenazate (Acramite), Spiromesifen, or Abamectin.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Hose down dusty plant foliage; avoid over-applying synthetic pyrethroids which kill beneficial predator bugs.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Small brown circular lesions with concentric rings and yellow halos that coalesce into large necrotic blights.
Tomato___Target_Spot.organic_treatment: Remove lower infected foliage; apply copper-based fungicides or bio-fungicides.
Tomato___Target_Spot.chemical_treatment: Fungicide rotation including Azoxystrobin, Pyraclostrobin, and Fluxapyroxad.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Maintain proper row spacing and stake plants to allow fast canopy drying.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves; curled, fern-like distorted leaf growth; stunted plant.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.organic_treatment: No cure exists once infected. Immediately remove and destroy infected plants. Wash hands with milk or soap before handling other plants.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.chemical_treatment: None available (viruses cannot be killed with chemical fungicides).
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Disinfect garden tools in 20% nonfat dry milk or bleach; prohibit tobacco smoking/vaping near plants; plant ToMV-resistant seeds.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaves become markedly stunted, erect, cup upward, and turn pale yellow at the margins; blossoms drop without setting fruit.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.organic_treatment: Cover seedlings with fine insect netting (mesh 50); install yellow sticky cards; apply insecticidal soap or neem oil to reduce whitefly vectors.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.chemical_treatment: Control whitefly populations with Imidacloprid, Dinotefuran, or Spiromesifen.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Plant TYLCV-resistant cultivars; eradicate nearby weed hosts that harbor whiteflies.
